name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jake Auchincloss running with large financial advantage ($7.3M cash vs. $1.3K)
Republican challenger raised only ~$26K with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Auchincloss holds a heavily Democratic seat, a massive cash advantage, and no serious funded opposition; markets price this near-certain for Democrats. The forecast stays at a Safe D margin of roughly 22 points.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Auchincloss or a polling surprise would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Auchincloss seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans about 11 points Democratic, in a strong Democratic year statewide. He has raised over $3.6 million and holds more than $7.3 million on hand, with no outside groups opposing him.

Republican Thomas Stalcup has raised roughly $26,000 and reports about $1,300 on hand, with no measurable outside support. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the funding gap makes this a Safe Democratic race.
